channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: LuxExperience CEO on Luxury Retail Customer Resiliency
item.description: Michael Kliger, CEO of LuxExperience, said the luxury market is becoming increasingly polarized, with affluent customers continuing to spend heavily while middle-class shoppers pull back under inflationary pressure. He said the company is less concerned about total active customers, which are around 900,000, than about growing the small group of top customers that generate a disproportionate share of sales. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Amazon Says AI Models Should Be Released When ‘Ready and Safe’
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. said artificial intelligence models should be released only after rigorous testing, weighing in on the debate about the pace of AI development after top labs called for a slowdown following safety lapses.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day

item.title: UN Must Unlock Its Doors to AI Industry: UNGA President
item.description: United Nations General Assembly president Khalilur Rahman speaks with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick. This week United Nations Secretary General said nations must coordinate global efforts to regulate AI, echoing calls for closer monitoring of the technology after warnings from leaders of the world’s top firms. The comments come days before world leaders descend on New York for the UNGA’s annual high-level week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: will.i.am on Personal AI Agents, Fundraising Efforts
item.description: Grammy-Award winning artist will.i.am sits down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick from Dreamforce to discuss his efforts to develop personal AI agents for college students, and the fundraising efforts around his company, FYI.AI (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Palantir CEO Says AI Firms Responsible for Their Own Actions
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc. Chief Executive Officer Alex Karp said developers of artificial-intelligence systems need to be held liable for their own work as opposed to depending on government regulation.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Martin

item.title: SpaceX May Buy Data From Failed Startups for AI Models
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX has held internal discussions about buying customer and operational information from troubled or defunct startups, according to people familiar with the matter. That data could help improve its artificial intelligence models. Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Four Big Deals That Reveal the State of Podcasting
item.description: New ventures involving ‘Giggly Squad,’ NPR, Steven Bartlett and Serial Productions have set the podcasting world atwitter
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: Anthropic's Warning of Existential Risk Hijacks Larger AI Debate
item.description: Some experts worry that heated rhetoric makes it hard to hold companies accountable, and sets back attempts to deal with environmental impact and job loss
item.dc:creator: Davey Alba and Rachel Metz

item.title: AI Pioneer Andrew Ng Calls Extinction Fears ‘Science Fiction’
item.description: Artificial intelligence pioneer Andrew Ng said warnings about existential AI risks from researchers at top model makers are “science fiction” that may be detrimental to ensuring the technology’s maximum benefits to society.
item.dc:creator: Micah Barkley

item.title: AI Wealth Boom and Silicon Valley's Jobless Tech Workers
item.description: As the global AI debate heats up, another major AI-related discussion is roiling the US tech capital: Who is reaping the financial benefits of the AI boom, and who is missing out? As the coming IPOs of Anthropic and OpenAI are set to bring wealth to San Francisco, a recent gathering of laid-off workers highlight the flip side of the AI boom. Bloomberg's California reporter Francesca Maglione joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Case for AI Guardrails Without a Slowdown
item.description: AI is helping companies build faster, but as competition at the frontier intensifies, should there be limits on how much risk companies can take to stay ahead? Karen McCormick, chief investment officer at Beringea, argues the answer isn't slowing innovation, but establishing common guardrails around testing, cybersecurity, and incident reporting. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI’s Safety Debate Meets Silicon Valley FOMO
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down OpenAI's new plan to track when things go wrong after revealing new cases of its AI models going off-script. Plus, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi and machine learning pioneer Andrew Ng weigh in on the global AI safety debate. Meanwhile in Silicon Valley, the immediate fear is missing out on the money. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Extinction Fears Are ‘Science Fiction’: Andrew Ng
item.description: AI pioneer Andrew Ng is pushing back against renewed warnings that increasingly powerful models could pose an existential threat to humanity, calling those fears “much more science fiction than science.” He argues that AI systems will never be perfectly predictable, but that testing, safeguards, and engineering, can make them safer over time. He also warns that broadly slowing AI development could also slow progress on safety. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI ‘Existential Risk’ Is Close to Zero: Databricks CEO
item.description: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi is pushing back on fears that AI poses an existential threat to humanity, calling that risk “close to zero” while warning that the technology presents a very real and growing cybersecurity challenge. He discusses why AI is dramatically shortening the time it takes attackers to exploit vulnerabilities, how Databricks is preparing for those threats, and why the current period of rapid technological change reinforces his preference to keep the company private for now. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Venezuela Unblocks Media, Some Sites Still Dark
item.description: Venezuela began lifting years-long blocks on news websites, but some remain dark.
item.dc:creator: Andreina Itriago

item.title: This Is the Moment For AI Acceleration Says Nagda
item.description: In the last few weeks AI Leaders have urged a slow down in the rapid advancement of AI, while President Trump rebuffs these concerns. Danish Nagda, Founder and CEO at Rezilient Health joins to discuss the future of AI as well as Xi Jinping's upcoming visit to the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: King Charles III Urges AI Leaders to Protect Humanity at Summit
item.description:
Can technology leaders keep AI under control?
King Charles asked industry heads including Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis at his Scotland Summit, Shona Ghosh reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta-Tied Data Center Taps US Junk Bonds for the First Time
item.description: CleanSpark Inc. is seeking to borrow roughly $2.23 billion through a debut junk-bond offering to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure tied to Meta Platforms Inc..
item.dc:creator: Gowri Gurumurthy

item.title: Nvidia CEO Calls for AI Safety Tests at King Charles Summit
item.description: Titans of the artificial intelligence industry gathered in Scotland to hear Britain’s monarch challenge them to control their inventions.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen, Tom Mackenzie and Shona Ghosh

item.title: Apple, OpenAI and Qualcomm Leaders to Attend Trump-Xi Dinner
item.description: Apple Inc. Executive Chairman Tim Cook, OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman and Qualcomm Inc. head Cristiano Amon are poised to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping next week.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary, Mark Gurman and Ian King
